tls_invalid.title: TLS certificate is invalid
tls_invalid.description: The HTTPS certificate could not be verified.
tls_invalid.impact: Visitors may see a warning or be unable to connect securely.
tls_invalid.fix: Renew or replace the certificate, serve the complete certificate chain, and confirm the hostname matches.

missing_https.title: Site is served without HTTPS
missing_https.description: The scanned address uses unencrypted HTTP.
missing_https.impact: Visitors' traffic can be read or changed in transit.
missing_https.fix: Enable HTTPS with a valid certificate and redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS.

tls_expiring.title: TLS certificate expires soon
tls_expiring.description: The certificate is close to its expiry date.
tls_expiring.impact: An expired certificate interrupts secure access.
tls_expiring.fix: Renew the certificate and verify automatic renewal is working.

missing_hsts.title: HSTS header is missing
missing_hsts.description: HTTPS responses do not instruct browsers to stay on HTTPS.
missing_hsts.impact: A visitor may be downgraded to an insecure connection on a later visit.
missing_hsts.fix: Send Strict-Transport-Security on HTTPS responses after confirming every subdomain supports HTTPS.

missing_csp.title: Content Security Policy is missing
missing_csp.description: The page does not declare which sources may load scripts and other content.
missing_csp.impact: Injected content may be easier to run in a visitor's browser.
missing_csp.fix: Add a nonce-based Content-Security-Policy and allow only the sources your app needs.

missing_frame_protection.title: Framing protection is missing
missing_frame_protection.description: Neither frame-ancestors nor X-Frame-Options blocks unwanted embedding.
missing_frame_protection.impact: Another site could place your page in a deceptive frame.
missing_frame_protection.fix: Set frame-ancestors in CSP or send X-Frame-Options: DENY.

missing_content_type_options.title: Content type sniffing is not blocked
missing_content_type_options.description: The X-Content-Type-Options header is missing or does not say nosniff.
missing_content_type_options.impact: Browsers may interpret a response as a different content type.
missing_content_type_options.fix: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response.

weak_referrer_policy.title: Referrer Policy is missing or weak
weak_referrer_policy.description: The site does not limit information sent in the Referer header.
weak_referrer_policy.impact: Page paths may be disclosed to other sites.
weak_referrer_policy.fix: Use Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin or a stricter policy.

missing_permissions_policy.title: Permissions Policy is missing
missing_permissions_policy.description: Browser features are not explicitly restricted.
missing_permissions_policy.impact: Embedded or third-party content may request features the page does not need.
missing_permissions_policy.fix: Send a Permissions-Policy that disables unused features such as camera and microphone.

insecure_cookie.title: Cookie lacks Secure
insecure_cookie.description: A cookie on an HTTPS page is missing the Secure attribute.
insecure_cookie.impact: The cookie may be sent over an unencrypted connection.
insecure_cookie.fix: Set Secure on cookies used by the application.

cookie_missing_httponly.title: Session cookie lacks HttpOnly
cookie_missing_httponly.description: A session-like cookie is readable by JavaScript.
cookie_missing_httponly.impact: Injected scripts may be able to read the cookie.
cookie_missing_httponly.fix: Set HttpOnly on server-managed session cookies.

cookie_missing_samesite.title: Cookie lacks SameSite
cookie_missing_samesite.description: A cookie does not declare a SameSite policy.
cookie_missing_samesite.impact: The cookie may be sent in cross-site requests in some browsers.
cookie_missing_samesite.fix: Set SameSite=Lax or Strict unless a cross-site flow requires None.

cors_wildcard_credentials.title: CORS uses wildcard with credentials
cors_wildcard_credentials.description: The response combines a wildcard origin with credential sharing.
cors_wildcard_credentials.impact: Browsers reject this combination; it often signals a mistaken CORS configuration.
cors_wildcard_credentials.fix: Allow specific trusted origins and review whether credentials are needed.

cors_reflected_origin.title: CORS reflects an arbitrary origin
cors_reflected_origin.description: The site reflects an untrusted Origin while allowing credentials.
cors_reflected_origin.impact: An attacker-controlled site may read authenticated responses.
cors_reflected_origin.fix: Compare Origin against an explicit allowlist before sending credentialed CORS headers.

exposed_env_file.title: Environment file appears public
exposed_env_file.description: A server environment file was returned from a public path.
exposed_env_file.impact: Configuration and secrets may be exposed.
exposed_env_file.fix: Remove the file from the web root, block dotfiles, and rotate any exposed credentials.

exposed_git.title: Git metadata appears public
exposed_git.description: The public site returned a Git HEAD file.
exposed_git.impact: Repository history or source code may be recoverable.
exposed_git.fix: Block .git paths at the edge or web server and remove repository metadata from deployments.

exposed_backup.title: Backup archive appears public
exposed_backup.description: A ZIP backup was returned from a common public path.
exposed_backup.impact: Source code or private data may be downloadable.
exposed_backup.fix: Remove backups from the web root and use private storage.

directory_listing.title: Directory listing is enabled
directory_listing.description: A public directory lists its files.
directory_listing.impact: Visitors can discover files that were not intended to be advertised.
directory_listing.fix: Disable auto-indexing and serve only intended files.

open_redirect.title: Open redirect detected
open_redirect.description: A common redirect parameter accepts an external destination.
open_redirect.impact: Attackers can use your domain to lead visitors to another site.
open_redirect.fix: Accept only relative paths or destinations on a strict allowlist.

missing_security_txt.title: security.txt is missing
missing_security_txt.description: No valid security contact was found at the standard path.
missing_security_txt.impact: Researchers may have difficulty reporting vulnerabilities privately.
missing_security_txt.fix: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with a Contact field and an expiry date.

mixed_content.title: HTTPS page loads HTTP resources
mixed_content.description: The page references an insecure script, image, stylesheet, or frame.
mixed_content.impact: Some resources may be blocked or modified in transit.
mixed_content.fix: Load every embedded resource over HTTPS.

third_party_script_no_sri.title: Third-party script lacks integrity
third_party_script_no_sri.description: An external script tag has no Subresource Integrity hash.
third_party_script_no_sri.impact: A changed third-party script could run unreviewed code on your page.
third_party_script_no_sri.fix: Pin stable third-party scripts with integrity and crossorigin attributes, or host them yourself.

exposed_source_map.title: Production source map is public
exposed_source_map.description: A JavaScript source map is available from a public asset path.
exposed_source_map.impact: Application source and implementation details may be easier to inspect.
exposed_source_map.fix: Disable public browser source maps or keep them in private error-reporting storage.

client_secret_leak.title: Server secret appears in client code
client_secret_leak.description: A server-only secret name and value pattern was found in a public bundle.
client_secret_leak.impact: Anyone can download public client bundles and extract the value.
client_secret_leak.fix: Remove the secret from client code, move its use to a server-only module, and rotate it.

unauthenticated_api.title: Sensitive API response is public
unauthenticated_api.description: A common API path returned unauthenticated JSON with sensitive field names.
unauthenticated_api.impact: Private records may be accessible without signing in.
unauthenticated_api.fix: Enforce authentication and ownership checks in the route handler, then review returned fields.

exposed_next_data.title: Next.js data endpoint exposes sensitive fields
exposed_next_data.description: A public _next/data response contains sensitive field names.
exposed_next_data.impact: Page data may be readable without the intended access check.
exposed_next_data.fix: Authorize data requests on the server and avoid serializing private data into public page props.

vulnerable_next_version.title: Next.js version matches an advisory
vulnerable_next_version.description: A detected version falls in a published affected range.
vulnerable_next_version.impact: The deployment may be exposed if the advisory's conditions apply.
vulnerable_next_version.fix: Review the linked advisory and upgrade to a patched Next.js release.

middleware_auth_signal.title: Review dashboard access control
middleware_auth_signal.description: A dashboard page returned account-like markers without a session.
middleware_auth_signal.impact: This signal needs manual review before treating it as an authorization issue.
middleware_auth_signal.fix: Check authentication in the page, server actions, and route handlers; do not rely on middleware alone.

service_role_leak.title: Supabase elevated key appears public
service_role_leak.description: A service-role or secret key pattern was found in public code.
service_role_leak.impact: An elevated key can bypass database access policies.
service_role_leak.fix: Revoke and rotate the key immediately, then use it only in server-only code.

anon_readable_sensitive_table.title: Sensitive table is readable anonymously
anon_readable_sensitive_table.description: An anonymous one-row HEAD request can see at least one row in a sensitive-looking table.
anon_readable_sensitive_table.impact: Visitors may be able to read private records.
anon_readable_sensitive_table.fix: Enable row-level security and add narrowly scoped ownership policies using the real owner column.

anon_readable_table.title: Table permits anonymous reads
anon_readable_table.description: An anonymous one-row HEAD request can see a row.
anon_readable_table.impact: This may be intentional for public data; verify the table contains no private information.
anon_readable_table.fix: Review the table's intended visibility and its row-level security policies.

write_policy_manual.title: Write access needs manual verification
write_policy_manual.description: The scanner did not attempt INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE because those methods can change data.
write_policy_manual.impact: Anonymous write access cannot be ruled out by a safe remote scan.
write_policy_manual.fix: Review INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE grants and row-level security policies in Supabase.

exposed_sensitive_rpc.title: Sensitive-looking RPC is exposed
exposed_sensitive_rpc.description: An RPC name in the public OpenAPI schema suggests a privileged operation.
exposed_sensitive_rpc.impact: The function may be callable by anonymous users if grants are broad.
exposed_sensitive_rpc.fix: Review EXECUTE grants and enforce authorization inside the function; revoke anonymous access if unnecessary.

public_storage_bucket.title: Storage bucket is public
public_storage_bucket.description: A bucket is marked public in storage metadata.
public_storage_bucket.impact: Files may be available to anyone who knows their path.
public_storage_bucket.fix: Confirm the bucket is meant for public assets and keep sensitive files in private buckets.

public_storage_sensitive_path.title: Public bucket has sensitive-looking names
public_storage_sensitive_path.description: Anonymous listing returned object names that look private.
public_storage_sensitive_path.impact: The names may reveal where sensitive files are stored.
public_storage_sensitive_path.fix: Review the listed objects without downloading them and move private files to a private bucket.

open_signups.title: Public signups are enabled
open_signups.description: The authentication settings allow new public accounts.
open_signups.impact: This is expected for many products; confirm it matches your signup policy.
open_signups.fix: Disable public signups if accounts should be invite-only.

auth_autoconfirm.title: Email auto-confirmation is enabled
auth_autoconfirm.description: New email accounts may be marked verified without proving mailbox ownership.
auth_autoconfirm.impact: Attackers may register addresses they do not control.
auth_autoconfirm.fix: Require email confirmation in Supabase Auth settings.

weak_auth_provider.title: Anonymous auth provider is enabled
weak_auth_provider.impact: This is safe only when policies explicitly account for anonymous users.
weak_auth_provider.fix: Review anonymous-user policies or disable the provider if unused.

cross_user_read.title: Test account can read another user's row
cross_user_read.description: A second test account could see a row owned by the first account using a read-only HEAD request.
cross_user_read.impact: Authenticated users may be able to access each other's data.
cross_user_read.fix: Add an owner-scoped SELECT policy and verify it with two separate test accounts.

cross_user_manual.title: Cross-user access needs manual verification
cross_user_manual.description: The read-only test could not establish an owned row or sign in both test accounts.
cross_user_manual.impact: The scanner cannot confirm isolation from the available evidence.
cross_user_manual.fix: Prepare two dedicated test accounts and an owned test row, then review RLS policies.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q0: Can I check a site before signing up?
faq.a0: Yes. The free public check reads only the site's public response and headers. It does not run deeper probes or test your database.
faq.q1: Why do I need to verify ownership?
faq.a1: Ownership verification limits deeper checks to sites you control. You can verify with a DNS TXT record, a meta tag or a file under .well-known.
faq.q2: Will the scanner change my data?
faq.a2: No. SiteGuard uses read-only requests for automated checks. When a safe write-access determination is impossible, it asks you to verify manually.
faq.a3: The three-day Pro trial ends in read-only mode if you have no subscription. Your prior reports remain available; choose a plan to resume scans.

howPage.title: A repeatable way to reduce risk
howPage.intro: SiteGuard makes each check explainable: what was observed, why it matters and what to change.

steps.title: Establish ownership
steps.body: Add a public URL. Prove control using DNS TXT, a meta tag or a verification file. Unverified sites receive passive checks only.

steps.title: Run bounded checks
steps.body: Verified scans run small read-only steps across general web, Next.js and Supabase modules. Every request uses SSRF checks, timeouts and size limits.

steps.title: Act on changes
steps.body: Review findings, mark accepted risks, compare scans and receive alerts for new high-severity issues and regressions.

howPage.scoreIntro: Every scan starts at {score}. A confirmed finding subtracts its registry weight. Informational findings carry no penalty.
howPage.scoreDecay: If the same issue appears on multiple distinct assets, each additional occurrence contributes {percent}% of the previous one. Duplicate fingerprints count once.
howPage.scoreLimits: Penalties are summed, rounded to the nearest integer and never take the score below zero. The score is deterministic for the same findings; it is a prioritization aid, not a guarantee of security.
howPage.exampleNote: Weights come directly from the scanner registry and may change as checks evolve.
howPage.scopeTitle: What a scan can and cannot say
howPage.scopeBody: Automated checks reveal observable signals. They cannot prove that every path is secure. We never write to a target database to test access; uncertain write permissions are flagged for manual review.

security.title: Careful by design
security.intro: A security product should be clear about its own boundaries. These are the controls built into SiteGuard.

items.title: Verified scope
items.body: Deep scans require ownership verification and are paused when periodic re-verification fails. The public widget checks only passive signals.

items.title: Bounded network access
items.body: The scanner accepts HTTP or HTTPS on standard ports, blocks internal and metadata addresses, pins resolved IPs, validates redirects and caps time and response size.

items.title: Read-only inspection
items.body: Database checks use minimal read-only requests. Row contents are never stored; write access is never tested by modifying customer data.

items.title: Data boundaries
items.body: Supabase row-level security limits user access. Service credentials stay in server-only code, while supplied secrets are encrypted with versioned AES-256-GCM keys.

items.title: Protected delivery
items.body: Session checks, rate limits, optional bot verification, signed webhooks and a restrictive content security policy protect application flows.

items.title: Controlled sharing
items.body: Report links use unguessable revocable tokens and redact sensitive evidence. Scan history follows the retention period of the active plan.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.description: The agreement governing access to and use of SiteGuard.

sections.title: 1. Agreement and eligibility
paragraphs: These Terms form an agreement between you and the service provider identified below when you create an account, purchase a plan or use SiteGuard. If you act for an organization, you confirm that you have authority to bind it. You must be legally able to enter this agreement and provide accurate account information.

We may update these Terms when our service or legal obligations change. We will give reasonable notice of material changes through the product or by email. Continued use after the effective date means you accept the updated Terms; if you disagree, stop using the service and close your account.

sections.title: 2. Service and scope
paragraphs: SiteGuard provides automated, limited security checks, monitoring, reports and related tools for websites you control. Results reflect observable signals at the time of a scan. They do not constitute a penetration test, security certification, legal advice or a promise that a site is free of vulnerabilities.
Features, limits, scan frequency and retention vary by plan. We may change a feature to protect the service or comply with law, while seeking to preserve the core value of a paid subscription.

sections.title: 3. Your account and authorized targets
paragraphs: You are responsible for your account, users you invite, credentials and all activity under your account. Keep access details confidential, use appropriate authentication controls and notify us promptly of suspected compromise.

You may add and verify only sites that you own or are expressly authorized to assess. Ownership verification does not transfer legal rights. You must comply with the Acceptable Use Policy and obtain any consent required for scanning your infrastructure, customers or third-party services.

sections.title: 4. Trials, subscriptions and payment
paragraphs: A new eligible account receives one three-day Pro trial. When it expires without a subscription, scanning and other write actions stop while permitted historical views remain available. Paid subscriptions renew for the selected monthly or annual period unless canceled according to the billing flow.

Paddle is the merchant of record for payments, tax calculation, receipts and invoices. Prices are shown in EUR; applicable taxes are presented at checkout. Changes, cancellations and refunds are governed by the checkout terms and mandatory consumer law. Cancellation normally takes effect at the end of the current paid period. We may suspend paid features for overdue payments after reasonable notice.

sections.title: 5. Your content and our license
paragraphs: You retain ownership of site information, submitted configuration, reports derived from your scans and content you provide. You grant us a limited license to process this material solely to operate, secure, support and improve the service as described in the Privacy Policy and applicable data processing agreement.

SiteGuard, its software, design and documentation remain our intellectual property or that of our licensors. We grant you a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the service during your account's active term, subject to these Terms.

sections.title: 6. Confidentiality and security
paragraphs: Each party must protect the other's non-public information with reasonable care and use it only to perform this agreement. This duty excludes information that is public without breach, independently developed or lawfully received from another source. Disclosure required by law is permitted with notice where lawful.

We use technical and organizational safeguards described on the Security page. You remain responsible for the security of your applications and for deciding whether and how to apply a suggested fix. Report links are shareable by anyone holding the link until revoked; review redaction before sharing.

sections.title: 7. Availability and changes
paragraphs: We aim to provide a reliable service but do not guarantee uninterrupted availability or that any scan will detect every issue. External networks, target configuration and third-party services can affect results. Scheduled maintenance and emergency action may temporarily interrupt access.

We may impose reasonable rate limits, pause a scan that risks a target or our systems, and change operational controls to prevent abuse. We will use reasonable efforts to explain material service interruptions.

sections.title: 8. Suspension and termination
paragraphs: You may stop using SiteGuard and request account deletion through settings. You should export information you need before deletion. We may suspend or terminate access for a material breach, unauthorized scanning, fraud, security risk, legal requirement or persistent non-payment; where practical, we will notify you and allow a cure period.

On termination, your right to use the service ends. We delete or retain data as described in the Privacy Policy, subject to legal and operational requirements. Clauses that by nature should survive, including payment obligations, intellectual property, liability and dispute terms, remain effective.

sections.title: 9. Warranties and liability
paragraphs: To the extent permitted by law, the service is provided with reasonable care but without a guarantee of uninterrupted or error-free operation, fitness for a particular security outcome, or detection of every vulnerability. Nothing here excludes rights that cannot lawfully be excluded.

To the extent permitted by law, neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss, lost profits or lost data arising from this agreement. Our aggregate liability for claims relating to the service is limited to fees you paid for it in the 12 months before the event giving rise to the claim. These limits do not apply to fraud, willful misconduct, unpaid fees or liability that law forbids limiting.

sections.title: 10. Disputes and contact
paragraphs: Before formal proceedings, please contact us with a description of the concern so we can attempt to resolve it. Applicable law and competent courts are determined by the service provider's place of establishment, except where mandatory consumer protection law requires otherwise.
The legal entity, address and contact email below identify the service provider. Electronic notices about your account may be sent to the email address you provide.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: How SiteGuard collects, uses, protects and shares personal data.

sections.title: 1. Controller and scope
paragraphs: The service provider named below is the controller of account, billing contact, website visitor and support data. For personal data contained in a customer's scan configuration or results, we generally act as processor on the customer's instructions. This policy covers the website, application and related communications.
Contact the address below for privacy questions or requests. Where we process data as a processor, submit rights requests first to the customer that controls the relevant site or workspace.

sections.title: 2. Data we collect
paragraphs: We collect account details such as name, email, locale, role and authentication metadata; billing identifiers and status from Paddle; support and contact messages; preferences; site URLs and ownership proofs; scan metadata, scores, findings and limited technical evidence; team invitations; API key metadata; and security and access logs.

Automated Supabase checks store table and column names, access indicators and at most a row-count estimate. They do not store row contents. User-supplied test credentials and integration URLs are encrypted. Payment card details are handled by Paddle and are not stored by SiteGuard.

sections.title: 3. Purposes and legal bases
paragraphs: We process data to deliver accounts, scans, reports, billing and support under our contract; to protect the service, prevent abuse and keep essential records under legitimate interests; to meet tax, accounting or legal duties; and, where required, on your consent for optional cookies or non-essential communications.
You can withdraw consent at any time without affecting prior lawful processing. You may opt out of non-essential emails using the link in those messages or your notification settings.

sections.title: 4. Sharing and sub-processors
paragraphs: We share data only as needed to operate the service, comply with law or follow your direction. Our service providers are Supabase (database, authentication and storage), Vercel (hosting and serverless execution), Resend (transactional email), Paddle (payments, invoices and tax as merchant of record) and Cloudflare Turnstile when enabled (bot verification). Their processing is limited to their role and subject to appropriate contractual and security controls.

A current sub-processor list and data processing agreement (DPA) are available on request at the contact address below. We will provide notice of material sub-processor changes where required by our DPA and a reasonable opportunity to object under its terms.

sections.title: 5. International transfers
paragraphs: These providers may process information outside your country. Where a transfer requires a safeguard, we rely on applicable adequacy decisions, standard contractual clauses or another lawful mechanism, together with supplementary measures where appropriate. Contact us for information about the mechanism relevant to your data.

sections.title: 6. Retention and deletion
paragraphs: Scan history is retained according to your plan: 30 days on Starter, 90 days on Pro and 365 days on Agency, subject to operational purge schedules. We retain account data while the account is active and delete it after a verified deletion request, except for information needed for legal compliance, billing records, security investigations or dispute resolution.

You can request a data export or delete your account in settings. Backups and system logs may remain for a limited operational period before rotation. We do not use scan evidence to train public AI models.

sections.title: 7. Security
paragraphs: We use row-level database access controls, encrypted storage for supplied secrets, restricted service credentials, rate limits and secure transport. Access is limited according to role and purpose. No online service can guarantee absolute security; notify us promptly if you suspect misuse of your account.

sections.title: 8. Your rights
paragraphs: Depending on applicable law, you may request access, correction, deletion, portability, restriction or objection to processing, and may complain to a supervisory authority. We may need to verify your identity and may decline a request where a lawful exception applies. Account export and deletion tools are available in settings.

sections.title: 9. Cookies and communications
paragraphs: Essential cookies support authentication, locale, theme and consent preferences. Optional cookies or similar technologies are used only after consent where required; see the Cookie Notice for details and controls. Service messages necessary for account, security or billing may still be sent when you opt out of marketing or optional alerts.

sections.title: 10. Children and updates
paragraphs: SiteGuard is intended for professional users and is not directed to children. Do not submit children's personal data unless you have an appropriate lawful basis and contract with us for that processing.
We may update this policy as the service or law changes. Material changes will be communicated through the product or email. The effective date above identifies the current version.

acceptable-use.title: Acceptable Use Policy
acceptable-use.description: Rules for safe, authorized use of SiteGuard and its scanner.

sections.title: 1. Authorized use only
paragraphs: Use SiteGuard only for websites and systems you own or have explicit, current permission to assess. You are responsible for confirming that your agreement with a host, client or provider allows the chosen checks. Do not attempt to bypass ownership verification or domain blocks.

sections.title: 2. Prohibited conduct
paragraphs: Do not use the service to attack, disrupt, enumerate or exfiltrate from a third party; scan government, banking, major platform or other blocked targets without authorization; submit internal or metadata addresses; or use another person's account or API key without permission.

Do not upload malware, malicious links, illegal content or live third-party credentials; interfere with rate limits or service availability; reverse engineer access controls; or use findings to facilitate unauthorized exploitation.

sections.title: 3. Safe scanning boundaries
paragraphs: Automated checks are bounded and read-only. Do not use supplied test credentials unless they belong to dedicated accounts you control and their use is permitted. Never treat a positive or negative automated result as permission to perform intrusive testing. Coordinate more invasive work directly with the target owner.

sections.title: 4. Data and communications
paragraphs: Do not place sensitive personal data or secrets in site names, support messages, webhook URLs or publicly shareable reports unless strictly necessary. Respect others' privacy and intellectual property. Keep alert destinations under your control and use unsubscribe controls appropriately.

sections.title: 5. Enforcement
paragraphs: We may rate-limit, pause or remove sites, revoke keys, suspend access or report unlawful activity if we reasonably believe this policy is breached or systems are at risk. Where safe and practical, we will explain the action and allow an appeal through the contact address below.

sections.title: 6. Reporting abuse
paragraphs: If you believe a SiteGuard user is scanning without authorization or misusing the service, contact us with the site, relevant dates and a concise description. Avoid sending live secrets or unrelated personal data. We will review reports and take proportionate action.

cookies.title: Cookie Notice
cookies.description: The cookies and similar storage SiteGuard uses, and your choices.

sections.title: 1. Essential storage
paragraphs: SiteGuard uses essential cookies to keep you signed in, protect sessions, remember your language and theme, and store your cookie choice. These are necessary for the requested service or for remembering an express preference. They are used without optional-cookie consent where law permits.

Session cookies are generally short-lived or renewed as needed; the language and consent preferences may persist for up to one year. You can delete cookies in your browser, though signing in and preferences may stop working until recreated.

sections.title: 2. Optional technologies
paragraphs: We do not load optional analytics or advertising trackers unless you choose to allow them. Allowing optional cookies records your preference but does not itself activate a tracker when none is configured. If optional tools are introduced later, they will remain inactive until appropriate consent and this notice will identify their purposes and providers.

sections.title: 3. Third-party verification
paragraphs: When bot verification is enabled on a public form, Cloudflare Turnstile may process device and network signals to distinguish automated traffic. Its challenge is loaded only where the form is shown. Cloudflare's own notices explain its processing; disabling essential security verification may prevent form submission.

sections.title: 4. Your choice
paragraphs: Use the controls below to allow optional cookies or keep only essential ones. You can change your choice at any time. Withdrawing consent does not affect processing that took place before the change. Browser settings may also block or remove cookies.

sections.title: 5. Contact and changes
paragraphs: Contact us at the address below for questions about cookies. We will update this notice if our storage practices change, with the new effective date shown above.
